subject: Operational scenarios & region pin request — data residency and temporary egress
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational scenarios & region pin request — data residency and temporary egress

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme Health is actively evaluating Redwood for clinical note embeddings and runtime classification for our triage flow. Before we proceed to procurement we need a clear operational commitment on regional anchoring and allowed transient processing windows. Our legal and security teams have a few concrete asks: 

- Can Redwood commit to region pinning per-tenant (EU / US / APAC) for all model inference and caching?
- If transient cross-region processing is required (maintenance/failover/burst), can you define a maximum time window (we typically ask for explicit limits rather than "as needed") and notification/telemetry that will be provided?
- What is your subprocessor roster and how will we be notified of activations that could affect routing?
- We need confirmation of KMS behavior for customer-managed keys (BYOK) and whether keys ever leave the pinned region for key rollover or escrow.

Attached is our procurement checklist to help guide the conversation (ACME_Procurement_Checklist.pdf).

Can you send an operational runbook (bulleted scenarios) with explicit time-bounded failover windows and a proposed acceptance clause we can include in the DPA? If possible, we prefer explicit 36–72 hour windows depending on scenario.

Appreciate it — Rachel
Legal & Privacy, Acme Health
[rachel.kim@acmehealth.com]

[Attachment: ACME_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational scenarios & region pin request — data residency and temporary egress

Rachel — thanks for the clear asks and for the checklist, very helpful. Attached is a concise operational runbook (redwood-operational-scenarios-v1.pdf) and our current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster.csv). Below is a summary of the scenarios and the explicit commitments we can provide today; we can tighten language into a DPA addendum if legal wants precise clauses.

Summary commitments (proposed):
- Tenant-level region pinning: Yes — customer can select a single region (EU/US/APAC) for primary inference and cache residency. Models, KV caches, and transient logs are anchored to the selected region by default.
- Temporary cross-region processing (approved scenarios only):
  * Planned maintenance: up to 36 hours with prior notice (email + Ops Slack).
  * Emergency failover (capacity/region outage): up to 72 hours; automatic failback and post-incident report within 48 hours of restoration.
  * Burst scaling to handle short spikes: up to 6 hours and instrumented in telemetry.
- Notification & telemetry: For any transient egress we will provide a notification email to the nominated security contact and an Ops report link (includes timestamps, source/target regions, affected routes).
- KMS / key residency: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) remain within the chosen region; key material is never exported outside the region for routine rotations. For exceptional operational needs (disaster recovery) we will only perform cross-region key escrow with explicit pre-authorized workflow and audit logs.
- Subprocessors: We attach the current roster and will provide 30 days notice prior to adding a new subprocessor that could affect routing.

Next steps: If this matches Acme's risk profile, we can draft a DPA addendum with the above language. Here is a DocuSign link to a draft acceptance clause we commonly use: https://redwood.app/docusign/ACME-3741

Attachments: redwood-operational-scenarios-v1.pdf (summary runbook), subprocessor_roster.csv

Let me know if you want us to shorten the planned maintenance window to 24 hours or reduce the emergency failover to 48. I copied our legal ops (laura.bennett@redwood.com) and product security (irene.choi@redwood.com) so we can tighten the language.

Best,
David
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
[david.kim@redwood.com]

[Attachment: redwood-operational-scenarios-v1.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)]
[Attachment: subprocessor_roster.csv (CSV, 12 KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational scenarios & region pin request — data residency and temporary egress

Thanks David — quick internal notes before we send the DPA wording to Acme: 

- Ops ask: confirm instrumented automatic fallback has a deterministic timeline for cache eviction and replay; we should state "automatic failback within 24–48 hours after primary region restored" rather than vague "automatic failback".
- Security ask (Irene): clarify TLS endpoint rotation and whether any control-plane metadata (not PII) may transit region borders for telemetry; propose we explicitly exclude customer data from control-plane telemetry exports.
- Legal ask (Marissa): recommend making the planned maintenance window 36 hours and emergency failover capped at 48 hours for healthcare customers as a negotiable concession; include an acceptance clause with a required 5-day post-incident report and remediation plan.

Irene — can you confirm whether we can commit to KMS material never leaving the anchored region except for a documented, customer-approved escrow workflow?

If we get those confirmations we should send an updated runbook to Acme with redlined DPA language.

- Laura
VP Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational scenarios & region pin request — data residency and temporary egress

David / team — thank you, this is helpful. We discussed internally and can provisionally accept the proposed runbook provided Redwood agrees to the following refinements before we execute the DPA addendum: 

1) Emergency failover cap: reduce to 48 hours for Acme Health (we need tighter limits for clinical workloads).
2) Planned maintenance: 36 hours maximum with 72-hour advance notification for scheduled major upgrades.
3) KMS: BYOK must remain in-region; any escrow for disaster recovery requires documented approval from Acme's security team and must be accompanied by an auditable key access log.
4) Subprocessor notice: 30 days prior notice + right to review; critical subprocessor changes that affect routing require a 14-day review window.

If you can confirm these points in writing we will ask procurement to circulate the DPA signature package. We also prefer the post-incident report to include TTLs for any cached artifacts and a simple inventory of what moved cross-region.

We appreciate the responsiveness — Rachel
Legal & Privacy, Acme Health

[Accepted provisions pending formal DPA language and signature: DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/docusign/ACME-3741]
